equation_request.abstract: Dynamically corrected gates are extended to non-Markovian open quantum systems where limitations on the available controls and/or the presence of control noise make existing analytical approaches unfeasible. A computational framework for the synthesis of dynamically corrected gates is formalized that allows sensitivity against non-Markovian decoherence and control errors to be perturbatively minimized via numerical search, resulting in robust gate implementations. Explicit sequences for achieving universal high-fidelity control in a singlet-triplet spin qubit subject to realistic system and control constraint are provided, which simultaneously cancel to the leading order the dephasing due to non-Markovian nuclear-bath dynamics and voltage noise affecting the control fields. Substantially improved gate fidelities are predicted for current laboratory devices.

specification.problem: Numerically search for a piecewise-constant single-qubit pulse sequence (effective singlet-triplet qubit, fixed gradient h0 about X plus controllable exchange J(t) about Z) that implements a target gate exactly while cancelling to first order the sensitivity to quasi-static gradient error delta_h and multiplicative exchange (voltage) noise eps; verify on a one-qubit statevector simulator.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One system qubit, no ancillas, N-segment piecewise-constant sequence, target = pi/2 rotation about one axis (e.g. X) as the smallest instance. Quasi-static noise only; first-order Magnus cancellation; the optimizer is run classically offline and the found parameters are fed into a fixed rx/rz circuit. Outside scope: non-quasi-static (colored) bath dynamics, filter-function treatment of time-dependent noise, realistic pulse-shape/bandwidth constraints, higher-order cancellation, the paper's specific sequences and fidelities.

first-order Magnus error vectors for bath and voltage noise

equations.label: Segment propagator
equations.description: Total propagator of the piecewise-constant sequence with static errors. Factor 1/2 convention on X is an assumption.
equations.justification: Concrete single-qubit model from the sketch for a singlet-triplet qubit; the abstract names only the noise types.
assumptions: Gradient error enters as an X term, exchange noise is multiplicative on J
Normalization of coefficients is a choice

equations.label: Toggling-frame error expansion
equations.latex: U(\delta_h,\epsilon)=U_0(T)\exp\!\big[-i(\delta_h\,\Omega_1^{(\delta)}+\epsilon\,\Omega_1^{(\epsilon)})+O(2)\big],\quad \Omega_1^{(\delta)}=\tfrac12\int_0^T U_0^\dagger X U_0\,dt,\ \ \Omega_1^{(\epsilon)}=\tfrac12\int_0^T J_0(t)\,U_0^\dagger Z U_0\,dt
equations.description: First-order Magnus error terms in the toggling frame for the quasi-static noise.
equations.abstract_quote: allows sensitivity against non-Markovian decoherence and control errors to be perturbatively minimized via numerical search
equations.justification: Perturbative minimization implies first-order error terms; explicit integrals are standard Magnus background applied to the assumed model.
assumptions: Sketch writes bath operator as Z; here the bath operator is the X gradient term given eq_1 — choose consistently when implementing

equations.label: Cost function
equations.description: Target-gate infidelity (for d=2, |Tr|^2/4 is the process fidelity) plus squared norms of first-order error vectors; C=0 means exact gate with first-order cancellation of both noises.
equations.justification: Proposed formulation of the numerical search objective; weighting is unspecified in the abstract.
assumptions: Bounds on J_k and tau_k enforced by the optimizer

equations.label: Robust-gate condition
equations.description: Conditions satisfied at a cost minimum of zero.
equations.abstract_quote: which simultaneously cancel to the leading order the dephasing due to non-Markovian nuclear-bath dynamics and voltage noise affecting the control fields
equations.justification: Simultaneous leading-order cancellation plus a high-fidelity gate implies these conditions.
assumptions: Exact solution exists for the chosen N and bounds

equations.label: Fidelity readout
equations.description: Fidelity swept over static errors; a plateau near zero error (1-F = O(error^4) for first-order cancellation in amplitude) confirms cancellation.

registers.name: q
registers.role: single effective singlet-triplet qubit, little-endian index 0, no ancilla

steps.description: Fix h0, bounds on J and tau, N and target (pi/2 X rotation); define the model of eq_1.
Classically compute the error vectors and cost; run random-restart BFGS or gradient descent until C is near 0.

Build the circuit: for each segment apply rz(J_k tau_k) for exchange and rx(h0 tau_k) for gradient (angles = 2*coefficient*tau, noting segments with both terms non-commuting are approximated by sequential rotation unless split via small Trotter steps; exact segments need a single axis-tilted rotation, realizable with u or rotation about tilted axis via basis changes).
For each static (delta_h, eps) in a grid, rebuild the circuit with perturbed angles and compare statevector with the target; compute fidelity map.

specification.measurement: Statevector comparison preferred (no measurements); alternatively measure qubit 0 in the Z basis after the sequence and estimate population, which only tests state fidelity for one input.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Offline optimization of pulse parameters; compute F over the (delta_h, eps) grid; check the plateau width relative to an uncorrected baseline sequence.
assumptions: Smallest instance chosen: one qubit, N around 4-8 segments, pi/2 X rotation target
Quasi-static noise, first-order cancellation, and the optimizer finds exact solutions
Segment with simultaneous J and h0 is a single rotation about axis (h0, 0, J) with angle tau*sqrt(h0^2+J^2)
